title: Defending at the speed of frontier AI: Why resilience, governance, and leadership matter more than ever
summary: Frontier AI is accelerating cyber risk—and testing leadership. Read how resilience, governance and faster decisions can help organizations keep pace.
body_markdown:
### Explore key topics in this blog


1. Pressure is expanding beyond the cybersecurity team
2. Why resilience matters more than ever
3. Governance is becoming a competitive advantage
4. Defending at the speed of AI
5. The path forward with frontier AI
6. Building resilience for the frontier AI era


As frontier AI models such as Anthropic's Claude Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol continue to advance, much of the discussion has focused on cybersecurity operations: How quickly can vulnerabilities be discovered? How rapidly can exploits be developed? How should security teams adapt? These questions matter, but they’re only part of the leadership challenge.


In his blog, Defending at the speed of frontier AI: Lessons from the Fable shutdown and what to do in the next 60 days, Pierre Le Calvez outlines practical actions organizations can take now to strengthen preparedness and resilience. The next challenge is broader.


What happens when cyber risk becomes less about technology alone and more about an organization's ability to make decisions, coordinate action, and adapt at speed? Increasingly, that is the challenge frontier AI presents.


## Pressure is expanding beyond the cybersecurity team


For years, cybersecurity leaders have focused on improving visibility through monitoring, threat intelligence, vulnerability scanning, and detection. Those investments remain essential, but frontier AI is changing where the pressure sits inside organizations.


As AI-assisted tools become better at discovering vulnerabilities, identifying weaknesses, and generating findings, the constraint increasingly shifts from discovery to decision velocity. Security teams may know about a vulnerability within minutes and understand its potential impact within hours. The harder question is whether the organization can decide, coordinate remediation, and implement mitigations quickly enough to keep pace.


In many organizations, the biggest delays no longer sit inside the security operations center. They sit in approval processes, competing business priorities, resource constraints, and fragmented ownership.


The bottleneck is increasingly organizational.


## Why resilience matters more than ever


That is why resilience is becoming such an important differentiator. Organizations often think of resilience as recovery after a cyber incident, but it starts much earlier.


Resilience is the ability to absorb pressure, adapt to changing conditions, and continue operating effectively when the unexpected happens. In a frontier AI environment, resilient organizations tend to share several characteristics:


> - Clear visibility into critical systems and dependencies
> - Clear ownership and knowledge of key decision-makers
> - Effective coordination across technology, security, operations, and business teams
> - Regular testing of response processes
> - A clear understanding of operational bottlenecks


Most importantly, resilient organizations can act quickly without sacrificing governance. That balance becomes more important as threat timelines continue to compress.


## Governance is becoming a competitive advantage


Frontier AI is also introducing new governance questions. Organizations are increasingly dependent on external software providers, cloud platforms, open-source components, and AI services, while also introducing AI-enabled capabilities into business processes and operations. Together, these shifts create new forms of operational dependency and risk.


**Boards and executive teams are increasingly asking questions such as:**


> - How do we govern AI adoption responsibly?
> - How do we maintain appropriate human oversight?
> - How do we manage AI-related third-party risk?
> - How do we balance innovation and pace with resilience?
> - How do we make decisions quickly while maintaining accountability?


**These aren’t purely technology questions. They’re leadership questions** .


The organizations adapting most effectively aren’t necessarily creating entirely new governance structures. Instead, they’re evolving existing risk, security, and resilience frameworks to reflect the realities of an AI-enabled operating environment.


## Defending at the speed of AI


The phrase "defend at the speed of AI" is becoming increasingly common across the cybersecurity industry. In practice, it means recognizing that human-scale processes alone may no longer be sufficient for machine-scale challenges.


Defensive applications of AI are already helping organizations improve threat detection, vulnerability analysis, code review, incident investigation, and remediation prioritization. Used appropriately, AI can help security teams process information faster, reduce manual effort, and accelerate response.


The goal, however, isn’t to remove people from the process. Human judgment, accountability, and governance remain essential. The most effective organizations combine AI-assisted speed with disciplined oversight and operational control.


The objective isn’t full autonomy. It’s faster, better-informed decision-making.


## The path forward with frontier AI


Much of the attention surrounding frontier AI has focused on the capabilities of the models themselves. The more important question may be how organizations choose to respond.


The fundamentals of cybersecurity remain remarkably consistent:


> - Reduce unnecessary exposure
> - Strengthen identity controls
> - Improve visibility
> - Accelerate remediation
> - Test response plans
> - Understand dependencies
> - Modernize legacy environments where the risk justifies investment


What changes is the speed and discipline with which these activities must now operate. Organizations that strengthen resilience, improve governance maturity, and increase operational readiness will be better positioned, regardless of which AI model or technology emerges next.


The future of cybersecurity won’t be defined solely by better tools. It’ll be defined by better leadership, stronger operational discipline, and the ability to adapt confidently as technology continues to evolve.


In the age of frontier AI, resilience is no longer only a cybersecurity objective. It’s becoming a core business capability.
